title: An LV2 bundle carries the manifest a host discovers it by

needles: a built LV2 bundle carries the manifest a host discovers it by

installed_sdk.rationale: core/format/include ships with the SDK, and lv2_entry.hpp gains an exported entry: PULP_LV2_PLUGIN now emits pulp_lv2_write_bundle_ttl alongside lv2_descriptor, so every plug-in built from this header exports one more C symbol. What an LV2 bundle CONTAINS changes with it -- _pulp_add_lv2 writes manifest.ttl and <binary>.ttl beside the shared object -- which turns an artifact no host could discover into a plugin.

needles: int pulp_lv2_write_bundle_ttl(const char* bundle_dir, const char* binary)

offline_timeline_cli.rationale: No CLI verb, flag or handler is added or changed. The emitter runs from the build as a POST_BUILD step, never from a shipped command.

offline_timeline_mcp.rationale: No MCP tool definition or handler is added or changed. Nothing under tools/mcp reads or drives LV2 bundle packaging.

live_product_control.rationale: No capability, operation, executor binding or profile policy changes; nothing a live product can invoke is added, removed or re-gated. The controls this delivery makes reachable are LV2's own host-facing lv2:ControlPorts, which the generator already emitted per parameter and which shipping the manifest merely makes visible to a host -- a different surface from Pulp's control plane. Pulp's agent-facing control endpoint is deliberately unchanged and remains Standalone-only: _pulp_attach_control_shipping still forces production-stripped with empty capabilities for every non-Standalone format. Widening that would also change VST3, AU and CLAP, so it is its own decision and is recorded as an open question rather than taken here.

design_time_agent_manifest.rationale: docs/status/agent-capabilities.json is byte-identical and the capability contract reports fresh: the same 111 capabilities and 496 public headers, none added, removed or re-keyed. Packaging an existing format's bundle publishes no new design-time capability.
